Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. This synchronous30-second HTTP timeout is not a real-world execution deadline guarantee.

candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation: reduce orders when pipeline is high and inventory is sufficient, to avoid over-ordering and upstream backlog. For node0, if pipeline >= 20 and inventory >= 10, reduce order by 2. For node1, if pipeline >= 20 and inventory >= 8, reduce by 2. For node2, if pipeline >= 20 and inventory >= 25, reduce by 2. This is a conservative correction to prevent excessive pipeline buildup.

Demand-responsive increase: if recent demand exceeds baseline (growth > 1.1), increase orders to build inventory, but only if backlog is low and pipeline is not too high. For node0, if growth > 1.1 and backlog == 0 and pipeline < 30, increase by 2. For node1, if growth > 1.1 and backlog == 0 and pipeline < 30, increase by 2. For node2, if growth > 1.1 and backlog == 0 and pipeline < 30, increase by 2. This aims to preemptively stock up during demand surges.

rules.when: agent == 0 and growth > 1.1 and backlog == 0 and pipeline < 30
agent == 1 and growth > 1.1 and backlog == 0 and pipeline < 30
agent == 2 and growth > 1.1 and backlog == 0 and pipeline < 30

candidates.explanation: Backlog mitigation: if backlog is positive, increase orders to clear it, but only if pipeline is not excessive. For node0, if backlog > 0 and pipeline < 25, increase by 3. For node1, if backlog > 0 and pipeline < 25, increase by 3. For node2, if backlog > 0 and pipeline < 25, increase by 3. This prioritizes service level when backlogs exist.

It slightly increases orders at all nodes when recent demand is below baseline, aiming to build a modest buffer against a potential demand surge. The correction is kept small to avoid creating excessive inventory or backlog, and it is applied uniformly to maintain pipeline balance.

This rule set focuses on pipeline-aware relaxation. It reduces orders when the pipeline is already high relative to recent demand, preventing over-ordering and potential upstream backlog. Conversely, it increases orders when the pipeline is low, ensuring adequate supply. The correction is bounded to avoid large swings.

This rule set targets downstream service by increasing orders at upstream nodes when downstream backlog is present, while slightly reducing orders at downstream nodes to avoid exacerbating upstream backlog. It uses a small correction to coordinate the supply chain and improve service levels without causing instability.

Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.

Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.

Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each. candidates.explanation: Pipeline-aware relaxation: when recent demand is below baseline and inventory is ample, reduce orders to avoid excess inventory and upstream backlog. For node0, if inventory is low and backlog exists, increase order to recover service. For node1 and node2, if inventory is high and pipeline is low, reduce order to prevent overstock.

Coordinated demand-following: when recent demand exceeds baseline (growth>1.2), increase orders at all nodes to prevent stockouts. When growth is low and inventory is high, decrease orders to reduce holding costs. Node0 prioritizes backlog clearance.

Pipeline smoothing: adjust orders based on pipeline coverage. If pipeline is low relative to recent demand, increase order; if pipeline is high, decrease. Node0 also considers backlog. This aims to maintain steady flow and avoid oscillations.

messages.content:
Design bounded correction rules for a frozen HAPPO serial inventory policy.
Nodes: 0 disaster dispensing point, 1 regional warehouse, 2 upstream supply center.
Unchanged simulator: each period external demand plus node0 backlog is served from its inventory and pipeline arrival.
Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.
You are notified a demand emergency HAS occurred. Future demand, duration and magnitude are unknown. You only see past demand and current state. Do not infer knowledge of the event end. HAPPO does not train.
Return JSON {"candidates":[{"explanation":"...","rules":[{"when":"expression","delta":"expression"}]}]}.
User specifies candidate count (3 initial, 1 refinement). Each rule set contains1..4 ordered first-match rules evaluated separately for each node.
Expression features ONLY: agent, inventory, backlog, pipeline=sum of known in-transit, arrival=next known arrival, incoming=last observed local demand, recent=last5 external mean, baseline=preceding20 external mean, growth=recent/baseline, happo=current proposed order.
Expressions <=300 characters may use numbers, + - * /, comparisons, and/or/not, conditional expressions, min/max2..6args, abs1arg. No other names, code, attributes, imports or containers.
Delta clipped[-6,6], rounded, added to HAPPO order and clipped0..20. Prefer small coordinated corrections and pipeline-aware relaxation. Rules run on fresh causal state for each period. Zero correction is valid.
For feedback, scores are uncertain causal forecast rollouts, not actual future results. Improve both cost and downstream service; do not exploit sample noise. Explain mechanics briefly, no markdown.
Report interval3: each delivered report aggregates3 completed external demands. The demand_mean is repeated3 times only as a reconstruction, never exact within-block demand. Node0 incoming/recent/baseline use delivered reconstruction. Upstream incoming is last executed downstream order. Current inventory, backlog, every pipeline slot, previous orders and current HAPPO proposal are visible. Emergency notification gives no start, magnitude or end. Memory resets each episode and contains only already observed states/orders/delivered reports. Observation changes do not prove a correction caused them. Search feedback is uncertain synthetic prediction; independent review is never supplied to you. Return exactly requested candidate count, one to four valid DSL rules each.
